metadata.title: How much dissipation can a multiscale layer cascade carry?
metadata.description:
Multiscale layer constructions give, or are announced to give, finite-time blowup for the porous media, Boussinesq and Euler equations with smooth forcing and, with fractional dissipation |∇|^α of order α < (22 − 8√7)/9, for the forced Navier-Stokes equations. Exponents here are in the |∇|^α convention, where classical viscosity is α = 2. We give two upper bounds on the exponent. The first holds for every design constant: layers growing at rate √A on a background gradient A cannot carry more than α = 1/2, and layers growing at rate A no more than α = 1. The second transcribes, with equation and page, the force estimates of the smooth-forcing Boussinesq and Euler designs: they certify only 5.3×10^−4 and 6×10^−8 at the published choices, and at most 9.0×10^−3 and 7.5×10^−3 when every constant is retuned, over ten times below the exponent reached with a rough force. Both use the amplitude system and the damping of one layer, tested against nonlinear simulation. Seven criteria are not met and one run is inconclusive: the window error of the single-layer rate at one angle and the growth of its unstable band; the two-scale slope; the steered cycle at its first parameters and on a curved background; and the two-layer handoff and its control (correlation 0.808 against 0.9). We also reconstruct the exponent budget behind the published threshold. Nothing here establishes blowup for any equation or improves any published threshold.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/analysis-pde/navier-stokes).
metadata.version_notes: Failed criteria are now reported: the slope of the two-scale handoff test is 1.36 times the prediction (criterion not met); the steered two-layer handoff reaches a correlation of 0.808 against a criterion of 0.9, and 0.509 at the largest separation (criterion not met; the base-only control discriminates in three of five runs); the steered cycle at the first chosen parameters is refuted (726-fold growth, Rayleigh-Taylor instability of the background); the dynamical handoff without steering is inconclusive. The verification section is now a table of every criterion with its numbers and what follows from it. The transcribed design bounds are checkable: the equation and page of every estimate of the two Alpöge-Buckmaster papers, their identifiers and hashes, the thirteen Euler coefficient quotients, and the displayed inequalities and arithmetic behind case (iii) of both theorems (4.48e-3 and 3.77e-3). A numerical-methods section gives grids, integrator, steps, domain, parameters, hardware, run times, code paths and commands, and the data section points to the repository test that guards the quoted numbers. Evidence marks [V], [D], [MV], [U], [C] are added throughout. Conventions are stated at every number: 3.12e-3 is in our convention (6.25e-3 in the |∇|^α convention), 0.0350 is in the |∇|^α convention, and the abstract names its convention. The measured agreement of the peak growth rate is 8.6e-5 at phi = pi/2 and 4.1e-5 at phi = pi/4 (the earlier text gave 4e-5 for both). The identity for the fractional Laplacian is stated for a single mode and its use for a multi-harmonic profile is marked as a conjecture; Theorem 3.1 gains the hypothesis that the background gradients are unbounded, with a remark on a stage-dependent frequency exponent. The status section reports the repository, toolchain, job counts, axiom lists and kernel replay times. The bibliography is corrected (titles of the Cordoba-Lain-Sanclemente-Martinez-Zoroa Boussinesq paper, of the Alpöge-Buckmaster-Coiculescu porous-media paper with its third author, and of the two OpenAI manuscripts) and gains URLs. Three figures are added from the result files. Content-bar pass: a related-work subsection states, for each construction and each announced result the paper depends on, the hypotheses and the conclusion as its abstract or main theorem gives them; an experimental-design subsection gives the question, the committed prediction and the pass criterion of every experiment; five algorithms (the integrating-factor Runge-Kutta step, the local growth-rate estimator, the localization test, the bisection for the critical exponent and the exhaustive search behind the design bounds) are written from the code with their parameters and costs; five figures are added from the result files (finite-horizon convergence of the cascade model, the steered cycle against its thresholds, the growth of the neighbouring modes in the refuted run, the handoff correlations and slopes of all seven runs, and the design ceilings against the number of controlled derivatives). The bibliography grows from 9 to 28 works, each cited where its hypotheses and conclusion are discussed. The Alpöge-Buckmaster-Coiculescu porous-media paper is cited with its arXiv identifier, 2609.16470 (the arXiv page matches the archived copy in title, authors, abstract and 57 pages, with a different file hash), and the name is spelled Alpöge throughout. The journal data of the Cordoba-Lain-Sanclemente-Martinez-Zoroa Boussinesq paper (Advances in Mathematics, volume 480, article 110480, November 2025) are confirmed on Crossref. Review fixes: the abstract is shortened to 238 words and counts every criterion not met (seven, with one inconclusive run); the sections required of a manuscript are present (Introduction, Related work, Problem formulation, Method, Theory, Experimental design, Results, Ablation, Discussion, Limitations, Reproducibility, Conclusions); the appendix tables print under their headings, before the bibliography. The single-layer rate error over the flat window at pi/4 (2.47 percent against 2) and the growth clause of the band prediction are reported as not met. The EXP-008 factor two is reported as a property of the closed forms and the measured ratio 1.812 is given; the horizon factor of the critical-exponent figure is corrected; the EXP-003 horizon gaps are stated at their three probe values; the statement that continuous integration checks the quoted numbers is replaced by what the test file checks and the fact that it is run locally; every row of the criteria table names the folder that records the run. Second pass: the description now equals the current abstract (seven criteria not met, one inconclusive run); the table of criteria is stated to be typed by hand from the result files; the quoted-numbers test is described as pinning the factor 945 only; the ablation row for the hold damping gives the measured difference 2.6e-6; the September constructions are described as announced results.
